name: h
reason: independent: Dropping `α = β` (keeping `p ≍ q`): the weakened statement holds in the set-theoretic model and at Sort 0 (propext), so it cannot be refuted; proving it needs α = β from (α → Prop) = (β → Prop) and Subtype p = Subtype q, i.e. injectivity of type formers, which is not provable in Lean (type-identity).

name: H'
reason: independent: type-identity (argument only): the dependent row asks for ∀ {s t : Set α}, (↑s = ↑t) → (x : ↑s) → s = t. Refuting it needs s ≠ t with a proof of the type equality {x // x ∈ s} = {x // x ∈ t}; for s ≠ t with different cardinalities the equality is refutable, and for equinumerous ones (e.g. {0} and {1} in ℕ) it is neither provable nor refutable in Lean. Proving the statement would in turn refute ↑({0} : Set ℕ) = ↑({1} : Set ℕ), which holds in models identifying equinumerous types, while the set-theoretic model satisfies the statement. So neither the statement nor its negation is provable (argument, not a Lean proof).

name: of_equiv
reason: independent: Without `of_equiv`, T' holds iff every Fintype type is literally `Option^n PEmpty` (take P α := ∃ n, α = Option^n PEmpty; conversely the induction principle covers exactly those types). Refuting T' needs a provable disequality such as Bool ≠ Option (Option PEmpty); proving it needs the equality. Equality of equinumerous types is neither provable nor refutable in Lean (type-identity, as in core/Std).
